pairs.difference: A: the vending machine is turned three-quarters, sits slightly left of center and fills most of the card height. It stands on a plain purple backdrop with nothing competing for attention. B: the ship's wheel faces straight on and sits dead center in a mirror-symmetric layout. It is fairly small (area 0.245, at the bottom of the real range), with even margins on every side. A sunburst and a wooden deck floor fill the lower third and draw attention away from the wheel. In the lessons, generated cards keep showing this shape: whole, centered, front-facing, with equal margins all round.
pairs.fix: Turn the ship's wheel three-quarters and tilt it slightly. Make it bigger so the handle tips come close to the left and right edges, and push it a little off center. Shrink the deck floor or drop it, and leave a simple soft backdrop.

pairs.difference: A: the roller-coaster cars and track sweep diagonally and are cut off by the left, top and bottom edges (margin 0). This matches the bold edge crop of the real lighthouse in the lessons. B: the window is seen straight on, centered and symmetric, and its frame is fully inside the card with even brick borders on all four sides. That is the tidy, whole-object framing the generated lesson cards show. It also fills more of the card than any real card (area 0.50).
pairs.fix: Show the window at a slight angle. Let one open shutter run past the card edge, push the window a little off center, and show less brick wall around it.

pairs.difference: A: the campfire sits whole, low and centered. A blue kettle, a log cabin in the top right corner and pine trees compete with it, so the card reads as a scene and not a single item. This matches the generated lighthouse lessons, where added life rings, plants and rocks fight the hero. B: the coin binoculars are big and placed right of center, the post is cut off by the bottom edge (margin 0), and the city skyline sits behind as a soft backdrop. This matches the real lighthouse's crop at the bottom edge.
pairs.fix: Make the campfire larger and let the logs and stones run off the bottom edge. Remove the kettle and the cabin, and keep only soft, blurred trees in the background.

pattern: Generated cards show the whole object, centered, often front-on and symmetric, with even margins on every side and no edge cropping. They also add props or scenery (rocks, kettles, cabins, floors) that compete with the hero. Real cards are framed more boldly: the hero is larger, angled and off center, and is often cut off by an edge.
